# v0.9.26 - Retries That Do Not Repeat Work, and a Reviewed Backlog

## What's Changed in v0.9.26

The review backlog of 0.9.25 and the fixes of two more review rounds (a Fable round on the batch, twice). A push whose verifying listing failed could delete a pack the remote relied on (AA25); a failed ref write left an empty folder that stopped every later fetch (AA10); and the retry layer re-sent a delete, a rename or an upload after it may have reached the server (AA32), which removed another client's ref in the reviewer's reproduction. The rest is a dropped connection that every handler now sees as an API error, a ref walk that backs off when the server throttles, and smaller wording and Windows fixes.

### Fixed
- **A push whose verifying listing fails no longer deletes a pack the remote already relied on** (ROADMAP AA25; review 68e81e5, fable-B1). A stale clone could re-upload a pack under a name the remote held; if the listing that verifies the upload then failed once, the helper removed that pack and every clone of the branch failed. Pack names are listed before the first upload, only a name that was not there or that the listing proved wrong is removed, and nothing is removed when the listing cannot be read.
- **A failed ref write removes the empty folders it made, including after a dropped connection** (ROADMAP AA10, AA26). A nested branch push made `refs/heads/<dir>/` before writing the ref; if the write failed, the empty folder stopped every later `git fetch` and `ls-remote` (measured on CE and Pro 13.0.29). Folders that were already there are never touched.
- **A server's `Retry-After` is slept for at most 10 seconds** (ROADMAP AA28; fable-C1). urllib3 slept the whole header three times per request, on the thread that renews the push lease.
- **`tracked_remote_names` works for a `--mirror` clone** (ROADMAP AA13): the hidden-branch warning never fired there.
- **A lease is also aged by the wall clock** (ROADMAP AA11): the monotonic clock stops during a suspend on Linux and macOS.
- **A restore that left a name out says so on its last line** (ROADMAP AA14, AA29): "verified byte-exact for the files written", including a case pair with identical bytes, and it no longer cuts a branch name.
- **Source paths past 260 characters on a Windows without long-path support** (ROADMAP AA17, AA22): the payload and staging stats and opens go through the extended-length form, and a directory a stat cannot reach inside an embedded repository is reported as unreadable instead of dropped with exit 0. The walks themselves stay plain (ROADMAP AA24).
- **A dropped connection or timeout on an API call is a `SeafileAPIError`** (ROADMAP AA27; fable H2.5). The handlers written `except SeafileAPIError` (the ref listing's retry, the cleanups) used to miss the raw `requests` exception; the session now wraps it once (`SeafileConnectionError`, also a `RequestException`, so older handlers keep working). Its text names the method and path, never the query.
- **A delete, rename or upload is no longer sent again after it may have reached the server** (ROADMAP AA32; review 402087a, fable2-B2, C2). urllib3 re-sent a DELETE and PUT by default and any request after an SSL error: one cleanup delete went out four times and removed a ref another client had written meanwhile, and a ref write with `attempts=1` arrived four times. Only GET, HEAD and OPTIONS are re-sent now; a refused connection (nothing sent) is still retried. A connection error names its cause again (AA33, fable2-B1).
- **A ref walk backs off when the server answers 429** (ROADMAP AA23). The server's per-user request rate is shared by every endpoint; a batch of ref reads that was answered 429 halves the next batch's workers and a clean batch adds one back, up to the ceiling.
- **A fetch from a linked worktree shares the clone's advertised-refs record** (ROADMAP AA31, fable-G9.1): it is kept under the common git directory, so the worktree no longer prunes what the main checkout would have kept.
- **A non-owner's `--payload-gc --payload-delete` on Pro is refused before the history is downloaded** (ROADMAP AA31, fable-E1).

### Changed
- `--dry-run` prints a Note when the real run would set another `core.ignorecase` (ROADMAP AA9). `gates.py --changed` follows test modules that import other test modules (AA16).

### Upgrading

Nothing about what is stored changes and no setting is renamed. Behaviours that may surface: see "Upgrading to v0.9.26" in `UPGRADING.md`; nothing needs a step from you.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
